sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西，这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: The outbreak of bird flu that is tearing through the nation's poultry farms is the worst in U.S.
sentences.zh: 席卷全国禽场的禽流感疫情是美国历史上最严重的一次。

sentences.en: history.
sentences.zh: 历史。

sentences.en: But scientists say it's now starting to spread into places and species it's never been before.
sentences.zh: 但科学家们表示，它现在开始蔓延到以前从未出现过的地方和物种身上。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Emily Anthes explains.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事艾米丽·安西斯将为您解读。

sentences.en: It's Monday, April 22nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月22日，星期一。

sentences.en: Emily, welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 艾米丽，欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: Happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: So, Emily, we've been talking here on The Daily about prices of things and how they've gotten so high, mostly in the context of inflation episodes.
sentences.zh: 那么，艾米丽，我们一直在《每日新闻》讨论物价以及它们为何变得如此之高，主要是在通货膨胀的背景下。

sentences.en: And one of the items that keeps coming up is eggs.
sentences.zh: 其中一个反复被提及的商品就是鸡蛋。

sentences.en: Egg prices were through the roof last year, and we learned it was related to this.
sentences.zh: 去年鸡蛋价格飞涨，我们了解到这与此有关。

sentences.en: Avian flu has been surging in the United States.
sentences.zh: 禽流感在美国激增。

sentences.en: You've been covering this.
sentences.zh: 你一直在报道这件事。

sentences.en: Tell us what's happening.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们发生了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I have been covering this virus for the last few years, and the bird flu is absolutely tearing through poultry flocks, and that is affecting egg prices.
sentences.zh: 是的，过去几年我一直在报道这种病毒，禽流感正在疯狂席卷家禽群，这影响了鸡蛋价格。

sentences.en: That's a concern for everyone, for me and for my family.
sentences.zh: 这对每个人来说都是个担忧，对我个人和我的家人也是如此。

sentences.en: But when it comes to scientists, egg prices are pretty low on their list of concerns because they see this bird flu virus behaving differently than previous versions have.
sentences.zh: 但对于科学家而言，鸡蛋价格在他们的担忧清单上排位很低，因为他们发现这种禽流感病毒的表现与以往的版本不同。

sentences.en: And they're getting nervous in particular about the fact that this virus is reaching places and species where it's never been before.
sentences.zh: 他们感到紧张，特别是由于这种病毒正在蔓延到以前从未出现过的地方和物种身上。

sentences.en: Okay, so bird flu, though, isn't new.
sentences.zh: 好的，不过禽流感并不是什么新鲜事。

sentences.en: I mean, I remember hearing about cases in Asia in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我记得90年代听说过亚洲有病例。

sentences.en: Remind us how it began.
sentences.zh: 提醒我们一下它是如何开始的。

sentences.en: Bird flu refers to a bunch of different viruses that are adapted to spread best in birds.
sentences.zh: 禽流感是指一系列适应在鸟类中传播的病毒。

sentences.en: Wild water birds, in particular, are known for carrying these viruses.
sentences.zh: 尤其是野生水鸟，众所周知是这些病毒的携带者。

sentences.en: And flu viruses are sort of famous for also being shapeshifters.
sentences.zh: 流感病毒也以善于“变形”而闻名。

sentences.en: So they're constantly swapping genes around and evolving into new strains.
sentences.zh: 所以它们不断地交换基因，进化成新的毒株。

sentences.en: And as you mentioned back in the 90s, a new version of bird flu, a virus known as H5N1, emerged in Asia.
sentences.zh: 正如你提到的，早在90年代，一种名为H5N1的新型禽流感病毒在亚洲出现。

sentences.en: And it has been spreading on and off around the world since then, causing periodic outbreaks.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，它一直在世界各地断断续续地传播，导致周期性的疫情爆发。

sentences.en: And how are these outbreaks caused?
sentences.zh: 这些疫情是如何引起的？

sentences.en: So wild birds are the reservoir for the virus, which means they carry it in their bodies with them around the world as they fly and travel and migrate.
sentences.zh: 野生鸟类是病毒的宿主，这意味着它们在飞行、旅行和迁徙过程中，将病毒携带在体内传播到世界各地。

sentences.en: And most of the time, these wild birds, like ducks and geese, don't even get very sick from this virus, but they shed it.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，像鸭子和鹅这样的野生鸟类甚至不会因为这种病毒而病得很重，但它们会排出病毒。

sentences.en: So as they're traveling over a poultry farm, maybe if they happen to go to the bathroom in a pond that the chickens on the farm are using
sentences.zh: 所以当它们飞越禽场时，如果它们恰好在农场鸡群使用的池塘里排泄，

sentences.en: or eat some of the feed that chickens on the farm are eating, they can leave the virus behind.
sentences.zh: 或者吃了农场鸡群正在吃的饲料，它们就会留下病毒。

sentences.en: And the virus can get into chickens.
sentences.zh: 病毒就会进入鸡群。

sentences.en: In some cases, it causes mild illness.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，它只会引起轻微的疾病。

sentences.en: It's what's known as low pathogenic avian influenza.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的低致病性禽流感。

sentences.en: But sometimes the virus mutates and evolves, and it can become extremely contagious and extremely fatal in poultry.
sentences.zh: 但有时病毒会发生突变和进化，在禽类中变得极具传染性和致命性。

sentences.en: Okay, so the virus comes through wild birds, but gets into farms like this, as you're describing.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以病毒通过野生鸟类传播，但正如你所描述的，进入了这样的农场。

sentences.en: How have farms traditionally handled outbreaks when they do happen?
sentences.zh: 农场通常是如何处理疫情爆发的？

sentences.en: Well, because this threat isn't new, there is a pretty well-established playbook for containing outbreaks.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为这种威胁并不新鲜，所以有一套相当成熟的控制疫情的方案。

sentences.en: It's sometimes known as stamping out.
sentences.zh: 有时被称为“扑杀”。

sentences.en: And brutally, what it means is killing the birds.
sentences.zh: 残酷地说，这意味着杀死这些鸟类。

sentences.en: So the virus is so deadly in this highly pathogenic form that it's sort of destined to kill all of the birds on a farm anyway once it gets in.
sentences.zh: 这种高致病性病毒非常致命，一旦进入农场，所有的鸟类注定都会死亡。

sentences.en: So the response has traditionally been to proactively depopulate or cull all the birds so it doesn't have a chance to spread.
sentences.zh: 因此，传统的应对措施是主动清群或扑杀所有鸟类，以防止其扩散。

sentences.en: So that's pretty costly for farmers.
sentences.zh: 这对农民来说代价很高。

sentences.en: It is, although the U.S.
sentences.zh: 确实，尽管美国

sentences.en: has a program where it will reimburse farmers for their losses.
sentences.zh: 有一个项目可以补偿农民的损失。

sentences.en: And the way these reimbursements work is they will reimburse farmers only for the birds that are proactively culled and not for those who die naturally from the virus.
sentences.zh: 这些补偿的运作方式是，他们只补偿主动扑杀的鸟类，而不补偿那些自然死于病毒的鸟类。

sentences.en: And the thinking behind that is it's a way to incentivize farmers to report outbreaks early.
sentences.zh: 背后的想法是，这是一种激励农民尽早报告疫情的方式。

sentences.en: So, okay, lots of chickens are killed in a way to manage these outbreaks.
sentences.zh: 所以，为了控制这些疫情，大量的鸡被杀死了。

sentences.en: So we know how to deal with them.
sentences.zh: 我们知道如何处理它们。

sentences.en: But what about now?
sentences.zh: 但现在呢？

sentences.en: Tell me about this new strain.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说这个新毒株。

sentences.en: So this new version of the virus, it emerged in 2020.
sentences.zh: 这种新版本的病毒出现在2020年。

sentences.en: After the deadly outbreak of the novel coronavirus, authorities have now confirmed an outbreak of the H5N1 strain of influenza, a kind of bird flu.
sentences.zh: 在新冠病毒致命爆发后，当局现在确认了H5N1流感毒株的爆发，这是一种禽流感。

sentences.en: And pretty quickly it became clear that a couple things set it apart.
sentences.zh: 很快人们就清楚地发现，有几点让它与众不同。

sentences.en: A bald eagle found dead at Carvin's Cove has tested positive for the highly contagious bird flu.
sentences.zh: 在卡文湾发现的一只秃鹰尸体检测出高传染性禽流感呈阳性。

sentences.en: This virus, for whatever reason, seemed very good at infecting all sorts of wild birds that we don't normally associate with bird flu.
sentences.zh: 出于某种原因，这种病毒似乎非常擅长感染各种我们通常不与禽流感联系在一起的野生鸟类。

sentences.en: He was kind of stepping and then falling over and using its wing to right itself.
sentences.zh: 它走着走着就摔倒了，还用翅膀支撑自己站起来。

sentences.en: Things like eagles and condors and pelicans.
sentences.zh: 比如老鹰、秃鹫和鹈鹕。

sentences.en: We've just lost a parliament of owls in Minneapolis.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚在明尼阿波利斯失去了一群猫头鹰。

sentences.en: Yeah, a couple high-profile nests.
sentences.zh: 是的，几个备受关注的巢穴。

sentences.en: And also, in the past, wild birds have not traditionally gotten very sick from this virus.
sentences.zh: 而且，在过去，野生鸟类通常不会因为这种病毒而病得很重。

sentences.en: And this version of the virus not only spread widely through the wild bird population, but it proved to be devastating.
sentences.zh: 而这个版本的病毒不仅在野生鸟类种群中广泛传播，而且被证明是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: They're washing up along the east coast of the country, from Scotland down to Suffolk.
sentences.zh: 它们被冲上该国东海岸，从苏格兰一直到萨福克。

sentences.en: We were hearing about mass die-offs of seabirds in Europe by the hundreds and the thousands.
sentences.zh: 我们听说欧洲成百上千的海鸟大规模死亡。

sentences.en: And the bodies of the dead dot the island wherever you look.
sentences.zh: 无论你往哪里看，死鸟的尸体都点缀着这座岛屿。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Okay, so then, as we know, this strain, like previous ones, makes its way from wild animals to farmed animals, namely to chickens.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么正如我们所知，这种毒株和之前的毒株一样，从野生动物传播到养殖动物，即鸡。

sentences.en: But it's even more deadly.
sentences.zh: 但它更致命。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And, in fact, it has already caused the worst bird flu outbreak in U.S.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它已经导致了美国历史上最严重的禽流感疫情。

sentences.en: history.
sentences.zh: 历史。

sentences.en: So more than 90 million birds in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以美国有超过9000万只鸟类

sentences.en: have died as a result of this virus.
sentences.zh: 死于这种病毒。

sentences.en: 90 million birds.
Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I should be clear that that represents two things.
sentences.zh: 我应该说明，这代表了两件事。

sentences.en: So some of those birds are birds who naturally got infected and died from the virus.
sentences.zh: 其中一些鸟类是自然感染并死于病毒的。

sentences.en: But the vast majority of them are birds that were proactively culled.
sentences.zh: 但绝大多数是主动扑杀的鸟类。

sentences.en: And what it adds up to is 90 million farmed birds in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 总计有9000万只美国养殖鸟类

sentences.en: have died since this virus emerged.
sentences.zh: 自这种病毒出现以来已经死亡。

sentences.en: And it's not just a chicken problem.
sentences.zh: 而且这不仅仅是鸡的问题。

sentences.en: Another thing that has been kind of weird about this virus is it has jumped into other kinds of farMs.
sentences.zh: 关于这种病毒的另一件奇怪的事情是，它已经跳跃到了其他种类的农场。

sentences.en: It is the first time we've seen a bird flu virus jump into U.S.
sentences.zh: 这是我们第一次看到禽流感病毒跳跃到美国

sentences.en: livestock.
sentences.zh: 牲畜身上。

sentences.en: It's now been reported on a number of dairy farms across eight U.S.
sentences.zh: 目前已在美国八个州的多个奶牛场报告了病例。

sentences.en: states.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是前所未有的。

sentences.en: And that's just something that's totally unprecedented.
sentences.zh: 所以它现在出现在奶牛场。

sentences.en: So it's showing up at dairy farms now.
sentences.zh: 你是说禽流感现在已经传播到牛身上了。

sentences.en: You're saying that bird flu has now spread to cows.
sentences.zh: 这是怎么发生的？

sentences.en: How did that happen?
sentences.zh: 我们不知道牛最初是如何被感染的。

sentences.en: So we don't know exactly how cows were first infected.
sentences.zh: 但大多数科学家的最佳猜测是，也许是一只迁徙的受感染野生鸟类将病毒排泄到了牛饲料、牧场或池塘中。

sentences.en: But most scientists' best guess is that maybe an infected wild bird that was migrating shed the virus into some cattle feed or a pasture or a pond.
sentences.zh: 然后牛接触到了它。

sentences.en: And cattle picked it up.
sentences.zh: 好消息是，它们似乎不像鸡那样病得那么重。

sentences.en: The good news is they don't seem to get nearly as sick as chickens do.
sentences.zh: 它们通常在几周内就能自行完全康复。

sentences.en: They are generally making full recoveries on their own in a couple of weeks.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以不需要大规模扑杀牛。

sentences.en: Okay, so no mass culling of cows.
sentences.zh: 不，目前看来没有必要。

sentences.en: No, that doesn't seem to be necessary at this point.
sentences.zh: 但坏消息是，看起来我们正在看到这种病毒在牛与牛之间传播。

sentences.en: But the bad news is that it's starting to look like we're seeing this virus spread from cow to cow.
sentences.zh: 我们还不知道具体是如何发生的。

sentences.en: We don't know exactly how that's happening yet.
sentences.zh: 但任何时候你看到牛与牛或哺乳动物之间的传播，这都是一个大问题。

sentences.en: But any time you see cow to cow or mammal to mammal transmission, that's a big concern.
sentences.zh: 这究竟为什么？

sentences.en: And why is that exactly?
sentences.zh: 嗯，原因有很多。

sentences.en: Well, there are a bunch of reasons.
sentences.zh: 首先，它可能使疫情规模变得更大、传播速度更快，这可能会增加对食品供应的风险。

sentences.en: First, it could allow the outbreak to get much bigger, much faster, which might increase the risk to the food supply.
sentences.zh: 我们还可能预计它会增加对农场工人的风险，即那些可能与这些病牛接触的人。

sentences.en: And we might also expect it to increase the risk to farm workers, people who might be in contact with these sick cows.
sentences.zh: 目前，接触这种病毒的农民将其传染给别人的可能性很低。

sentences.en: Right now, the likelihood that a farmer who gets this virus passes it on is pretty low.
sentences.zh: 但任何时候你看到哺乳动物之间的传播，都会增加病毒适应并可能在某一天变得擅长在人类之间传播的机会。

sentences.en: But any time you see mammal to mammal transmission, it increases the chance that the virus will adapt and possibly, maybe one day, get good at spreading between humans.
sentences.zh: 需要明确的是，目前没有任何证据表明这种情况正在牛群中发生。

sentences.en: To be clear, that's not something that there's any evidence of happening in cows right now.
sentences.zh: 但只要有牛与牛之间的传播发生，就足以让科学家们感到担忧。

sentences.en: But the fact that there's any cow to cow transmission happening at all is enough to have scientists a bit concerned.
sentences.zh: 如果我们更广泛地思考农场之外的情况，还有另一个巨大的危险潜伏在那里。

sentences.en: And then if we sort of think more expansively beyond what's happening on farms, there's another big danger lurking out there.
sentences.zh: 那就是当这种病毒进入野生动物体内时会发生什么。

sentences.en: And that's what happens when this virus gets into wild animals.
sentences.zh: 我们无法控制的庞大种群。

sentences.en: Vast populations that we can't control.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.

sentences.zh: 我编写了《Connections》游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的拼图之一。

sentences.zh: 那么艾米丽，你说另一个威胁是野生动物种群中的流感威胁。

sentences.en: So Emily, you said that another threat was the threat of flu in wild animal populations.
sentences.zh: 显然，它已经在野生鸟类中了。

sentences.en: Clearly, of course, it's already in wild birds.
sentences.zh: 它还去了哪里？

sentences.en: Where else has it gone?
sentences.zh: 嗯，它之所以成为如此大的威胁，是因为它在野生鸟类中传播得太广了。

sentences.en: Well, the reason it's become such a threat is because of how widespread it's become in wild birds.
sentences.zh: 所以它们几乎在所到之处不断地将病毒重新引入野生动物种群。

sentences.en: So they keep reintroducing it to wild animal populations pretty much anywhere they go.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到这种病毒反复出现在各种你可能认为会吃野生鸟类的动物身上。

sentences.en: So we've seen the virus repeatedly pop up in all sorts of animals that you might figure would eat a wild bird.
sentences.zh: 比如狐狸、短尾猫、熊。

sentences.en: So foxes, bobcats, bears.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至在北极熊身上看到了它，还有浣熊。

sentences.en: We actually saw it in a polar bear, raccoons.
sentences.zh: 所以很多食肉动物和食腐动物，人们认为这些动物可能会偶然发现生病或死亡的鸟类，吃掉它，从而感染病毒。

sentences.en: So a lot of carnivores and scavengers, the thinking is that these animals sort of might stumble across a sick or dead bird, eat it, and contract the virus that way.
sentences.zh: 但我们也看到它出现在一些更令人惊讶的地方。

sentences.en: But we're also seeing it show up in some more surprising places, too.
sentences.zh: 我们在宽吻海豚身上也发现了这种病毒，真没想到。

sentences.en: We've seen the virus in a bottlenose dolphin in all places.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And most devastatingly, we've seen enormous outbreaks in other sorts of marine mammals, especially sea lions and seals.
sentences.zh: 最令人痛心的是，我们目睹了其他种类的海洋哺乳动物，尤其是海狮和海豹，出现了大规模的疫情爆发。

sentences.en: So elephant seals, in particular in South America, were just devastated by this virus last fall.
sentences.zh: 因此，去年秋天，南美洲的象海豹遭受了这种病毒的毁灭性打击。

sentences.en: My colleague Apoorva Mandavili and I were talking to some scientists in South America who described to us what they called a scene from hell of walking out onto a beach in Argentina
sentences.zh: 我和同事阿普尔瓦·曼达维利（Apoorva Mandavili）与南美洲的一些科学家进行了交谈，他们向我们描述了在阿根廷海滩上看到的景象，称之为“地狱般的场景”——

sentences.en: that is normally crowded with chaotic, living, breathing, breeding elephant seals and the beach just being covered by carcass after carcass after carcass.
sentences.zh: 那里本应挤满了混乱、鲜活、呼吸着、繁衍着的象海豹，但海滩上却铺满了尸体，一具接着一具。

sentences.en: God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Mostly carcasses of young newborn pups.
sentences.zh: 大部分是刚出生幼崽的尸体。

sentences.en: The virus seemed to have a mortality rate of 95 percent in these elephant seal pups.
sentences.zh: 这种病毒在这些象海豹幼崽中的死亡率似乎高达95%。

sentences.en: And they estimated that it might have killed more than 17,000 of the pups that were born last year.
sentences.zh: 据估计，去年出生的幼崽中，可能有超过1.7万只死于这种病毒。

sentences.en: So almost the entire new generation of this colony.
sentences.zh: 几乎是这个种群整整一代的新生儿。

sentences.en: These are scientists that have studied these seals for decades and they said they've never seen anything like it before.
sentences.zh: 这些科学家研究海豹已经几十年了，他们说从未见过这样的惨状。

sentences.en: And why is it so far reaching, Emily?
sentences.zh: 艾米丽，为什么它的影响范围如此之广？

sentences.en: I mean, what explains these mass die-offs?
sentences.zh: 我是说，是什么导致了这些大规模的死亡？

sentences.en: There are probably a few explanations.
sentences.zh: 原因可能有几个。

sentences.en: One is just how much virus is out there in the environment being shed by wild birds into water and onto beaches.
sentences.zh: 首先是环境中存在的病毒数量巨大，野生鸟类将其排入水中并带到了海滩上。

sentences.en: These are also places that viruses like this haven't been before.
sentences.zh: 这些地方也是病毒以前从未涉足过的区域。

sentences.en: So it's reaching elephant seals and sea lions in South America that have no prior immunity.
sentences.zh: 因此，它传播到了南美洲那些此前从未接触过该病毒、毫无免疫力的象海豹和海狮身上。

sentences.en: There's also the fact that these particular species, these sea lions and seals, tend to breed in these huge colonies all crowded together on beaches.
sentences.zh: 还有一个事实是，这些特定的物种——海狮和海豹——往往聚集在海滩上庞大的群体中进行繁衍。

sentences.en: And so what that means is if a virus makes its way into the colony, it's very conducive conditions for it to spread.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，一旦病毒进入群体，就形成了非常有利于传播的条件。

sentences.en: And scientists think that that's actually what's happening now, that it's not just that all these seals are picking up the virus from individual birds,
sentences.zh: 科学家认为，现在发生的情况正是如此，不仅仅是所有海豹都从个别鸟类身上感染了病毒，

sentences.en: but that they're actually passing it to each other.
sentences.zh: 而是它们实际上在彼此传播。

sentences.en: So basically, this virus is spreading to places it's never been before, kind of virgin snow territory where animals just don't have the immunity against it.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这种病毒正在扩散到它从未去过的地方，就像一片处女地，动物们对它毫无免疫力。

sentences.en: And once it gets into a population packed on a beach, say, of elephant seals, it's just like a knife through butter.
sentences.zh: 一旦进入像象海豹这样聚集在海滩上的种群，病毒的传播就像热刀切黄油一样迅速。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And an even more extreme example of that is what we're starting to see happen in Antarctica, where there's never been a bird flu outbreak before until last fall.
sentences.zh: 一个更极端的例子是我们开始在南极洲看到的情况，直到去年秋天之前，那里从未发生过禽流感疫情。

sentences.en: For the first time, this virus reached the Antarctic mainland.
sentences.zh: 这是该病毒首次抵达南极大陆。

sentences.en: And we are now seeing the virus move through colonies of not only seabirds and seals, but penguin colonies, which have not been exposed to these viruses before.
sentences.zh: 我们现在看到病毒不仅在海鸟和海豹种群中蔓延，还波及到了此前从未接触过这些病毒的企鹅种群。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And it's too soon to say what the toll will be.
sentences.zh: 现在谈论最终的代价还为时过早。

sentences.en: But penguins also, of course, are known for breeding in these large colonies.
sentences.zh: 但当然，企鹅也以在大型群体中繁衍而闻名。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Probably don't have many immune defenses against this virus and, of course, are facing all these other environmental threats.
sentences.zh: 它们可能对这种病毒没有多少免疫防御能力，而且当然，它们还面临着所有其他环境威胁。

sentences.en: And so there's a lot of fear that you add on the stress of a bird flu virus and it could just be a tipping point for penguins.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们非常担心，如果再加上禽流感病毒的压力，这可能会成为企鹅生存的临界点。

sentences.en: Emily, at this point, I'm kind of wondering why more people aren't talking about this.
sentences.zh: 艾米丽，此时此刻，我有点纳闷为什么没有更多人在谈论这件事。

sentences.en: I mean, I didn't know any of this before having this conversation with you.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在和你交谈之前，我对这一切一无所知。

sentences.en: And it feels pretty worrying.
sentences.zh: 这感觉相当令人担忧。

sentences.en: Well, a lot of experts and scientists are talking about this with rising alarm.
sentences.zh: 嗯，许多专家和科学家正带着日益增长的警惕谈论这件事。

sentences.en: And in terms that are quite stark,
sentences.zh: 而且用词相当严峻，

sentences.en: they're talking about the virus spreading through wild animal populations so quickly and so ferociously that they're calling it an ecological disaster.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论的是病毒在野生动物种群中传播的速度之快、势头之猛，以至于称之为一场生态灾难。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: But that's a disaster that sometimes seems distant from us, both geographically.
sentences.zh: 但这灾难有时看起来离我们很遥远，无论是在地理上，

sentences.en: You know, we're talking about things that are happening maybe at the tip of Argentina or in Antarctica.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们谈论的事情可能发生在阿根廷的尽头或南极洲。

sentences.en: And also from our concerns of our everyday lives.
sentences.zh: 而且也远离我们日常生活的关切。

sentences.en: What's happening in penguins might not seem like it has a lot to do with the price of a carton of eggs at the grocery store.
sentences.zh: 企鹅身上发生的事情可能看起来与杂货店里一盒鸡蛋的价格没什么关系。

sentences.en: But I think that we should be paying a lot of attention to how this virus is moving through animal populations, how quickly it's moving through animal populations,
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们应该密切关注这种病毒如何在动物种群中移动，它在动物种群中移动的速度有多快，

sentences.en: and the opportunities that it is giving the virus to evolve into something that poses a much bigger threat to human health.
sentences.zh: 以及它给病毒提供了什么样的机会去进化成对人类健康构成更大威胁的东西。

sentences.en: So the way it's spreading in wild animals, even in remote places like Antarctica, that's important to watch, at least in part because there's a real danger to people here.
sentences.zh: 所以它在野生动物中的传播方式，即使是在南极洲这样偏远的地方，也值得关注，至少部分原因是这对我们人类确实存在真正的危险。

sentences.en: So we know that the virus can infect humans and that generally it's not very good at spreading between humans.
sentences.zh: 我们知道病毒可以感染人类，而且通常它在人与人之间的传播能力并不强。

sentences.en: But the concern all along has been that if this virus has more opportunities to spread between mammals, it will get better at spreading between them.
sentences.zh: 但一直以来的担忧是，如果这种病毒有更多机会在哺乳动物之间传播，它在哺乳动物间的传播能力就会增强。

sentences.en: And that seems to be what is happening in seals and sea lions.
sentences.zh: 而这似乎正是海豹和海狮身上正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: Scientists are already seeing evidence that the virus is adapting as it passes from marine mammal to marine mammal.
sentences.zh: 科学家们已经看到了证据，表明病毒在从一种海洋哺乳动物传播到另一种的过程中正在发生适应性演变。

sentences.en: And that could turn it into a virus that's also better at spreading between people.
sentences.zh: 这可能会使它变成一种在人与人之间传播能力更强的病毒。

sentences.en: And if somebody walks out onto a beach and touches a dead sea lion, if their dog starts playing with a sea lion carcass,
sentences.zh: 如果有人走到海滩上触摸了一只死海狮，如果他们的狗开始玩弄海狮的尸体，

sentences.en: you could imagine that this virus could make its way out of marine mammals and into the human population.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象这种病毒可能会从海洋哺乳动物传播到人类群体中。

sentences.en: And if it's this mammalian adapted version of the virus that makes its way out, that could be a bigger threat to human health.
sentences.zh: 如果这种经过哺乳动物适应的病毒版本传播出来，那对人类健康可能构成更大的威胁。

sentences.en: So the sheer number of hosts that this disease has, the more opportunity it has to mutate and the more chance it has to mutate in a way that would actually be dangerous for people.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种疾病拥有的宿主数量越多，它变异的机会就越多，以对人类危险的方式变异的可能性也就越大。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And in particular, the more mammalian hosts.
sentences.zh: 特别是哺乳动物宿主越多，

sentences.en: So that gives the virus many more opportunities to become a specialist in mammals instead of a specialist in birds, which is what it is right now.
sentences.zh: 这给了病毒更多机会成为哺乳动物的“专家”，而不是像现在这样只擅长感染鸟类。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I like that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个说法。

sentences.en: A specialist in mammals.
sentences.zh: 哺乳动物的专家。

sentences.en: So what can we do to contain this virus?
sentences.zh: 那么我们能做些什么来遏制这种病毒呢？

sentences.en: Well, scientists are exploring new options.
sentences.zh: 嗯，科学家们正在探索新的选择。

sentences.en: There's been a lot of discussion about whether we should start vaccinating chickens in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 关于我们是否应该开始在美国给鸡接种疫苗，已经有很多讨论了。

sentences.en: The government, USDA labs have been testing some poultry vaccines.
sentences.zh: 政府，即美国农业部的实验室一直在测试一些禽类疫苗。

sentences.en: It's probably scientifically feasible.
sentences.zh: 从科学上讲，这可能是可行的。

sentences.en: There are challenges there both in terms of logistics.
sentences.zh: 但在后勤方面存在挑战。

sentences.en: Just how would you go about vaccinating billions of chickens every year?
sentences.zh: 你究竟该如何每年为数十亿只鸡接种疫苗？

sentences.en: There are also trade questions.
sentences.zh: 还有贸易问题。

sentences.en: Traditionally, a lot of countries have not been willing to accept poultry products from countries that vaccinate their poultry.
sentences.zh: 传统上，许多国家一直不愿意接受来自给家禽接种疫苗的国家的禽肉产品。

sentences.en: And there's concern about whether the virus might spread undetected in flocks that are vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 而且人们担心病毒是否会在已接种疫苗的鸡群中未被察觉地传播。

sentences.en: So as we saw with COVID, the vaccine can sometimes stop you from getting sick, but it doesn't necessarily stop infection.
sentences.zh: 正如我们在新冠疫情中所看到的，疫苗有时可以阻止你生病，但不一定能阻止感染。

sentences.en: And so countries are worried they might unknowingly import products that are harboring the virus.
sentences.zh: 因此，各国担心它们可能会在不知情的情况下进口携带病毒的产品。

sentences.en: And what about among wild animals?
sentences.zh: 那么野生动物呢？

sentences.en: I mean, how do you even begin to get your head around that?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你甚至该如何着手处理这个问题？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, thinking about vaccinating wild animals maybe makes vaccinating all the chickens in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是说，考虑给野生动物接种疫苗，可能让给美国所有的鸡接种疫苗看起来都容易多了。

sentences.en: look easy.
sentences.zh: 关于有限的疫苗接种计划已经有一些讨论，但这在全球范围内是不可行的。

sentences.en: There has been some discussion of limited vaccination campaigns, but that's not feasible on a global scale.
sentences.zh: 所以不幸的是，底线是目前还没有好的方法来阻止病毒在野生动物中的传播。

sentences.en: So unfortunately, the bottom line is there isn't a good way to stop spread in wild animals.
sentences.zh: 我们可以尝试保护一些脆弱的种群，但我们无法阻止这种病毒的循环。

sentences.en: We can try to protect some vulnerable populations, but we're not going to stop the circulation of this virus.
sentences.zh: 所以，艾米丽，我们开始这次谈话是因为《每日新闻》对鸡蛋价格的好奇。

sentences.en: So, Emily, we started this conversation with a kind of curiosity that The Daily had about the price of eggs.
sentences.zh: 然后你向我们解释了禽流感。

sentences.en: And then you explained the bird flu to us.
sentences.zh: 不知怎的，我们最终了解了一场在我们周围展开的生态灾难，以及它可能是下一场人类大流行的源头。

sentences.en: And then somehow we ended up learning about an ecological disaster that's unfolding all around us and potentially the source of the next human pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这确实很可怕。

sentences.en: That is pretty scary.
sentences.zh: 这很可怕，而且很容易让人感到不知所措。

sentences.en: It is scary, and it's easy to get overwhelmed by it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我应该退后一步说，这一切并非不可避免。

sentences.en: And I feel like I should take a step back and say, none of this is inevitable.
sentences.zh: 这一切并不一定会明天就发生。

sentences.en: None of this is necessarily happening tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 但这就是为什么科学家们感到担忧，也是为什么他们认为密切关注农场内外发生的事情非常重要，因为这种病毒正在各种动物种群中传播。

sentences.en: But this is why scientists are concerned and why they think it's really important to keep a very close eye on what's happening both on farms and off farms as this virus spreads through all sorts of animal populations.
sentences.zh: 在我和研究禽流感几十年的专家们的采访中，反复出现的一点是，这种病毒总是让他们感到意外。

sentences.en: One thing that comes up again and again and again in my interviews with people who have been studying bird flu for decades is how this virus never stops surprising them.
sentences.zh: 有时是坏消息，比如象海豹的大规模死亡，以及对奶牛群的侵袭。

sentences.en: And sometimes those are bad surprises, like these elephant seal die-offs, the incursions into dairy cattle.
sentences.zh: 但最近也出现了一些令人鼓舞的迹象。

sentences.en: But there are some encouraging signs that have emerged recently.
sentences.zh: 我们开始看到一些初步证据，表明一些在早期接触过这种病毒后幸存下来的鸟类种群可能正在产生某种免疫力。

sentences.en: We're starting to see some early evidence that some of the bird populations that survived sort of early brushes with this virus might be developing some immunity.
sentences.zh: 所以这或许有助于减缓这种病毒在动物种群中的传播。

sentences.en: So that's something that maybe could help slow the spread of this virus in animal populations.
sentences.zh: 我们只是还不完全清楚事态将如何发展。

sentences.en: We just don't entirely know how this is going to play out.
sentences.zh: 流感是一个非常棘手、狡猾的敌人。

sentences.en: Flu is a very difficult, wily foe.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么科学家们试图如此密切、专注地关注正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: And so that's one reason scientists are trying to keep such a close, attentive eye on what's happening.
sentences.zh: 艾米丽，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Emily, thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该知道的消息。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 本次投票，赞成票366张，反对票58张。

sentences.en: On this vote, the yeas are 366 and the nays are 58.
sentences.zh: 法案通过。

sentences.en: The bill is passed.
sentences.zh: 周六，在四次连续投票中，众议院以压倒性多数通过了一揽子长期搁置的对乌克兰、以色列及其他美国盟友的援助计划，

sentences.en: On Saturday, in four back-to-back votes, the House voted resoundingly to approve a long-stalled package of aid to Ukraine, Israel, and other American allies,
sentences.zh: 这为拜登总统带来了一场重大胜利，他将对乌克兰的援助列为自己的首要任务之一。

sentences.en: delivering a major victory to President Biden, who made aid to Ukraine one of his top priorities.
sentences.zh: 本次投票，赞成票385张，反对票34张，一人投出席票。

sentences.en: On this vote, the yeas are 385 and the noes are 34, with one answering present.
sentences.zh: 法案无异议通过。

sentences.en: The bill is passed without objection.
sentences.zh: 众议院通过了这项950亿美元方案的组成部分，其中包括一项可能导致在全国范围内封禁TikTok的法案。

sentences.en: The House passed the component parts of the $95 billion package, which included a bill that could result in a nationwide ban of TikTok.
sentences.zh: 本次投票，赞成票311张，反对票112张。

sentences.en: On this vote, the yeas are 311 and the nays are 112.
sentences.zh: 法案通过。

sentences.en: The bill is passed.
sentences.zh: 哦，有一人投出席票。

sentences.en: Oh, one voting present.
sentences.zh: 我错过了，但谢谢你。

sentences.en: I missed it, but thank you.
sentences.zh: 在一场打破惯例的非凡举动中，民主党人介入并提供了关键票数，推动该立法克服了共和党强硬派的反对，并将其提交至众议院表决。

sentences.en: In a remarkable breach of custom, Democrats stepped in to supply the crucial votes to push the legislation past hardline Republican opposition and bring it to the floor.
sentences.zh: 众议院请保持秩序。

sentences.en: The House will be in order.
sentences.zh: 参议院预计最早将于周二通过该立法。

sentences.en: The Senate is expected to pass the legislation as early as Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由瑞奇·诺维茨基（Ricky Novetsky）、妮娜·费尔德曼（Nina Feldman）、埃里克·克鲁普克（Eric Krupke）和亚历克斯·斯特恩（Alex Stern）制作。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Ricky Novetsky, Nina Feldman, Eric Krupke, and Alex Stern.
sentences.zh: 由丽莎·周（Lisa Chow）和帕特里夏·威兰斯（Patricia Willans）编辑。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lisa Chow and Patricia Willans.
sentences.zh: 节目包含玛丽安·洛萨诺（Marian Lozano）、丹·鲍威尔（Dan Powell）、罗文·内米斯托（Rowan Nemisto）和索菲亚·兰德曼（Sophia Landman）的原创音乐，并由克里斯·伍德（Chris Wood）进行工程处理。

sentences.en: It contains original music by Marian Lozano, Dan Powell, Rowan Nemisto, and Sophia Landman, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格（Jim Brunberg）和本·兰兹维克（Ben Landsverk）创作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsverk of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢安德鲁·雅各布斯（Andrew Jacobs）。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Andrew Jacobs.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西（Sabrina Tavernisi）。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，该党就陷入了一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 在《Metro》的最新一期节目中，我和莎拉·凯尼格（Sarah Koenig）一起，讲述了人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我是莎拉·凯尼格，本期将讲述人们试图维持自身影响力却在过程中逐渐失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
